# Arbitrum Swap

> A self-custodial interface for swapping tokens on Arbitrum One. The wallet holds the keys, the user sets slippage and signs every order, and network gas is paid in ETH. No deposits, no account, no platform fee.

## Facts

- Network: Arbitrum One, chain ID 42161, public RPC https://arb1.arbitrum.io/rpc. Arbitrum Nova is a separate network with chain ID 42170.
- Gas: paid in ETH by the sending wallet. On Arbitrum a transaction fee has two components, documented by Arbitrum itself.
- Custody: self-custodial. Orders are cryptographically signed instructions from the user's account; nothing executes without that signature.
- Cost context: Arbitrum is an optimistic rollup — it compresses transaction data before posting it to Ethereum, which is why a swap costs a fraction of a mainnet swap.
- Slippage: set by the user before signing. It bounds the difference between the quoted and the executed price.
- The swap panel published on the page is a labelled preview: it fetches no quote and signs nothing.

## Independence

This page is published independently. Arbitrum and the Arbitrum logo belong to their respective owners. Swapping tokens carries risk, including loss of capital; nothing on the page is investment advice.

## Sources

- Arbitrum chain IDs and RPC endpoints: https://docs.arbitrum.io/build-decentralized-apps/reference/node-providers
- Arbitrum gas and fees: https://docs.arbitrum.io/how-arbitrum-works/deep-dives/gas-and-fees
- Ethereum transactions and signing: https://ethereum.org/developers/docs/transactions/
- Optimistic rollups and data compression: https://ethereum.org/developers/docs/scaling/optimistic-rollups/
